wallet.connectionHelp: Quick Setup creates a wallet on the Nostr WoT LNbits service, or the server chosen in Advanced settings. NWC (recommended) connects your existing wallet with its own permissions and spending limits. LNbits connects directly using your server URL and wallet Admin API key.
wallet.albyGuide: Alby Hub: create an NWC connection
wallet.lnbitsApiGuide: LNbits: find your wallet API key
wallet.lnbitsConnectionHint: For a direct LNbits connection, enter your instance URL and the Admin API key of the wallet you want to use. If you have an NWC connection URI, paste it in the NWC tab instead.
wallet.lnbitsAdminKeyHint: Open your LNbits wallet and reveal its keys under API info. The Admin API key authorizes spending from that wallet. It is not your LNbits login or server administrator password.
wallet.autoApproveHint: This amount caps each automatic payment and the total across all sites over 24 hours. Further payments ask for approval. Failed or uncertain attempts also count. Set 0 to always ask.

mutes.aboutBody: Mutes are people, words, hashtags and threads you want to hide in Nostr apps that support mute lists. This editor reads your NIP-51 mute list (kind 10000) from your relays and edits its public entries. Changes take effect after you publish. Encrypted private entries are preserved, but are not displayed or counted here.
mutes.ownListMissing: No published mute list was found on your relays. Add entries and publish to create one.
mutes.emptyList: Your published mute list is empty.
mutes.privateOnly: Your list has encrypted private entries. They are preserved, but cannot be displayed or counted here.
mutes.noPublicPeople: This list has no public people to import.
mutes.title: Mutes
mutes.readFailed: Could not read your mute list — no relay answered. Nothing has been changed.
mutes.cardInfo: Your NIP-51 mute list (kind:10000). Muted people, words and hashtags are published to your relays so every Nostr client you use hides them. Existing private mutes are preserved.
mutes.peopleHint: Add npub or hex public keys to mute. They will be hidden across Nostr clients that read your mute list.
mutes.wordsHint: Notes containing these words are hidden.
mutes.hashtagsHint: Notes with these hashtags are hidden.
mutes.importPlaceholder: npub or hex of list owner
mutes.importHint: Paste the public key of someone whose public mute list you trust. Their muted people are merged into yours, ready to publish.
mutes.noMuteListFound: No mute list found for this key
pqc.menuDesc: Keys that stay private even after secp256k1 is broken
pqc.reasonShortSeed: This account uses a {count}-word seed phrase. Post-quantum keys must come from a 24-word phrase — a shorter one carries only 128 bits of entropy, which would become the weakest link.
pqc.reason.read-only: This is a watch-only account. It has no private key, so it cannot hold post-quantum keys.
pqc.reason.remote-signer: This account signs through a remote signer, and that protocol has no post-quantum operations yet.
pqc.reason.no-seed: This account was imported from a private key, so there is no seed phrase to derive from.
pqc.independentHint: You can still add a standalone post-quantum key using the pqc:keygen command. It is not recoverable from a seed phrase, so you must back it up separately.
pqc.readyDesc: Your keys are derived from your 24-word seed phrase. Nothing extra to back up — the words you already wrote down restore them.
pqc.exportDesc: Saves a key file you can import here again, or keep as a backup.
pqc.exportWarnShort: This file can read your messages
pqc.exportWarn: It contains your secret keys. Anyone who gets a copy can decrypt post-quantum messages sent to you. Prefer the encrypted download, and store it somewhere only you can reach.
pqc.importedDesc: These keys came from a file you imported, not from your seed phrase. Keep your copy of that file safe.
pqc.importedBackupShort: Your seed phrase cannot restore this key
pqc.publishDesc: Publish this event to your relays so others can send you post-quantum encrypted messages. Until you do, senders fall back to classic encryption.
pqc.limits: This protects the confidentiality of messages sent from now on, permanently. It does not stop a quantum attacker from forging events in your name — that needs a signature migration, which is not part of this.
pqc.cardDesc: Publish a key so messages sent to you stay private even after today's cryptography is broken
pqc.published: Published to {sent} of {relays} relays. People can now send you post-quantum messages.
pqc.alreadyPublished: Your post-quantum keys are already published and up to date.
pqc.checkFailed: Could not check whether your keys are published — no relay answered.
pqc.staleAttestation: Your published keys no longer match this account. Publish again so senders use the right key.
pqc.importDesc: You can generate a standalone post-quantum key on your own machine and import it here. Nothing is sent anywhere — the generator runs offline, and you can read its source before running it.
pqc.importPaste: Paste your two secret keys (or the key file), or choose a file below
pqc.importedBackupWarning: This key is not recoverable from your seed phrase. If you lose your copy of the key file, messages sent to it can never be read again.
pqc.importRemoveConfirm: Remove this key? Anyone who already has your attestation will keep encrypting to it, and you will no longer be able to read those messages.
pqc.importFileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
perm.declinedDesc: Sites you chose not to connect. They cannot ask again until this expires — remove one to let it ask.
pqc.cardEnabledDesc: Others can send you messages that stay private even after today's cryptography is broken
pqc.cardStaleDesc: What you published no longer matches this account's keys, so senders would use the wrong one
pqc.cardImportDesc: This account can't derive one from its seed phrase, but you can generate one and import it
pqc.howStep1: Your post-quantum keys are worked out from the seed phrase you already have — nothing new to write down.
pqc.howStep2: You publish one small event to your relays announcing the public half. That event is the only way anyone can discover your key.
pqc.howStep3: Apps that support it encrypt to that key, combined with today's encryption — so the result is never weaker than what you have now.
pqc.howLimit: This protects messages sent to you from now on, permanently, including against someone storing them today to read later. It does not change how your events are signed.
key.ncryptsecExplainMore: The backup is a NIP-49 file: your private key encrypted with the password you choose. Any Nostr client that supports ncryptsec can restore from it — and anyone who gets the file without the password cannot.
key.ncryptsecNoRecovery: Nothing can recover this password — not us, not another client. If you lose it, the backup is unreadable.
network.publishedFound: Latest verified event found. R = read, W = write.
network.noPublishedEvent: No relay-list event found on the relays checked.
network.publishedUnavailable: Could not verify your published list. Try again.
activity.pubkeyFilterHint: Filter by the other person’s public key or a public key referenced in the event’s p tags. Enter all or part of the hexadecimal key. This does not select your signing account.
network.publishedEmpty: The published event contains no usable relays. Your local list will be kept.
wallet.refreshSettingsHint: Refresh wallet name, connection details, approval limit and Lightning Address
wallet.disconnectHint: Removes the saved wallet connection from this extension. Your wallet and funds stay with the provider; reconnect to use them here.
approval.rememberHint: Always allow saves permission for future requests of this type from this site.
account.removeSeedWarning: This account comes from your seed phrase. Removing it leaves other accounts from that seed available in this extension. To stop using this seed in this extension, remove every account derived from it. You can recover this identity using the same seed phrase and derivation path. Keep a backup of both.
wizard.customPathHint: The next unused standard path is selected automatically. A valid custom path updates the public-key preview without saving an account. Keep the exact path with your seed backup.
wizard.invalidDerivationPath: Enter a valid path, for example m/44'/1237'/0'/0/1.
wizard.networkPathHint: Uses the {network} ({convention}) registered path prefix. This creates a Nostr identity, not a wallet on that network. Avoid reusing a path already used by your wallet.
wizard.unknownPathHint: Valid custom path; no common network prefix recognized.
approval.accountMismatchReason: The website requested a signature from a different account than the one selected in the extension. Nothing was signed. Select the same account in the website and extension, then try again.
wizard.pqKeyRequiresAccount: This file contains only post-quantum keys, not a Nostr account key. Create or import your account first, then restore this file in Settings → Post-quantum key.
wot.title: Web of Trust (experimental)
wot.menuDesc: Optional local graph and oracle queries
wot.experimentalNotice: Experimental: graph results can be incomplete or outdated. Trust scores describe follow/mute relationships, not safety or endorsement.
wot.consent: Enabling makes window.nostr.wot available to connected websites with identity access.
wot.oracleDisclosure: Oracle queries send your public key and queried public keys to this server. Use an oracle you trust. Hybrid mode also sends queries when the local graph has no answer.
wot.partial: This graph reached a sync limit. Missing results do not mean no relationship exists.
wot.syncNotice: Sync downloads public follow and relay lists and refreshes your mutes. It runs manually unless automatic syncing is enabled. Relay-list queries use this local snapshot in every mode.
wot.mutes: Your muted accounts score zero and cannot contribute local trust paths. Only account mutes affect scores; muted words, hashtags and events do not.
wot.mutesUnavailable: Mute list not verified. Sync to load it; current scores may not include your mutes.
wot.privateMutesUnavailable: Private mutes could not be decrypted. Only public mutes are applied. Unlock a local signing account to include private mutes.
wot.localDesc: Calculate trust from the graph you sync on this device.
wot.remoteDesc: Ask your chosen oracle for trust relationships.
wot.hybridDesc: Use your local graph first, then ask the oracle when needed.
wot.reloadRequired: The background is running an older build. Reload the extension, then open it again.
wot.depthHint: 1 hop includes people you follow. 2 includes their follows; 3 goes one level further. More hops take longer to sync. Save and resync to expand your local graph.
wot.missingLists: Follow lists unavailable from your relays
wot.howModes: Local uses your downloaded graph. Remote asks your chosen oracle. Hybrid tries local data first. Oracle results are server claims, not verified follow events.
wot.howUpdates: Newer follow lists replace older ones, including removals. People no longer reachable from your account are removed on resync. Missing lists keep the last known copy; limits and missing data are shown.
wot.howPrivacy: Snapshots contain public follows and relay lists. Private mutes are decrypted locally when possible, never saved as plaintext in the graph or sent to an oracle. Connected sites may infer mutes from scores.
wot.scoringHint: Scores range from 0 to 1. Start with the weight for the shortest distance, then add a bonus for each extra shortest path, up to the bonus cap. The final score never exceeds 1. Weights must not increase with distance.
wot.muteOverride: Your muted accounts always score zero and cannot contribute local trust paths. Private mutes apply only when they can be decrypted; otherwise a warning is shown.
wot.autoSyncHint: Check the active account’s follow and mute lists once a day. Save to apply.
wot.databaseHint: One local graph per synced account. Sizes cover WoT graph storage only, excluding vault, wallet and shared caches. Approximate sizes are marked ≈.
wot.edgeLimitHint: Leave empty for Unlimited. Each follow relationship is one edge. Hop depth and any other limits you set still apply.
wot.authorLimitHint: Leave empty for Unlimited. Controls how many profiles can have their follow lists requested during one sync, not how many people appear in the graph.
wot.followsLimitHint: Leave empty for Unlimited. Controls how many follows to keep from each profile’s list.
wot.lookupHint: Check a public key using your saved query mode and scoring settings. Remote and hybrid lookups may contact your configured oracle.
wot.invalidPubkey: Enter a valid npub or 64-character hex public key.
wot.scoreUnavailable: No score is available within your configured graph depth.
wot.explanation.pathsHint: Each hop is one follow relationship. Paths are shortest routes and may share edges.
wot.explanation.formula: Distance points + path bonus = score. The bonus respects your limits; the total is capped at 100.
wot.explanation.noMutes: No account mutes in your loaded mute list.
wot.explanation.mutesExcluded: Your muted accounts are excluded from trust paths.
wot.explanation.privateUnavailable: Private mutes could not be read. Only known mutes were excluded.
wot.explanation.mutesUnavailable: Your mute list could not be verified. This result may not account for all your mutes.
wot.explanation.graphHint: These totals describe the saved graph, not just paths to this person.
wot.explanation.incomplete: The local graph is incomplete: some follow lists are missing or a configured limit was reached.
wot.explanation.local: Calculated from your saved local follow graph.
wot.explanation.oracle: Calculated from oracle results using your scoring settings. When mutes exist, only one returned path avoiding known mutes is credited.
wot.explanation.muted: This account is muted by you, so its score is zero.
wot.explanation.none: No eligible path was found within the search depth. This is not proof that no relationship exists.
wot.deleteDatabaseHint: Delete this saved social graph? Your account and keys are kept. You can sync the graph again.
wot.sharedCacheActionsHint: Public lists shared by all accounts. Resync refreshes lists through the active account. Deleting this cache keeps your saved account graphs.
wot.deleteCacheHint: Delete shared public-list cache? Your saved account graphs and keys are kept. Future syncs download the lists again.
approval.rememberDenyHint: Always reject blocks future requests of this type from this site.
approval.followReplacementWarning: {origin} is trying to replace your last known list of {count} follows with {newCount} contacts. Publishing this removes follows missing from the new list.
approval.followReplacementQuestion: Are you really sure? Cancel to review the request. Always allow does not skip this warning.
